clue.text: Seabird with cry like a fox on hickory tree

parts.note: the shag is a cormorant-like seabird
a fox's call is a bark

explanation.surface: A seabird screeching like a fox while perched in a hickory.
explanation.definitionFit: The shagbark is a North American species of hickory named for its peeling bark.

clue.text: Speak out about the remains, then move off casually

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one word wraps another

parts.note: to speak out is to say
ash is what remains after burning, as in cremation

explanation.surface: Someone delivers a eulogy over the ashes, then strolls off.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk with a casual, swaggering glide.

clue.text: Diminishes a writer

parts.note: H. E. Bates was an English novelist and short-story writer

explanation.surface: A complaint that some author is getting smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Abates means lessens or dies down, a synonym of diminishes.

clue.text: Had an injury covering skin, now brown and grey

indicators.note: covering means one word goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: someone hurt may have bled
rind is the skin of fruit or cheese

explanation.surface: A wound over the skin has left a bruise that is now brown and grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Brindled describes a coat streaked or flecked with brown and grey, as on some dogs and cattle.

clue.text: Noisy rabble — ringleader expelled

parts.note: the leader, or first letter, of the word ring
someone expelled is thrown out

explanation.surface: A rowdy mob whose instigator has been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' is read as 'ring' plus 'leader': the first letter of ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Rout is an old word for a disorderly crowd or mob.

clue.text: Lacking freshness can restrict British firm

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one word is held inside another

parts.note: something lacking freshness is stale

explanation.surface: A flat, uninspired company may curb a British business.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable and firm are synonyms meaning steady and secure.

clue.text: Arousing mistrust after losing the way? It's a platitude

indicators.note: arousing stirs things up, so the letters that remain are shaken into a new order
losing means a part is taken away from the word mistrust

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: Stirring up suspicion once you've lost your way is just a cliche.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after losing the way' takes ST from MISTRUST to leave MISTRU; 'Arousing' then rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A truism is a statement so obviously true it is a cliche, which is what a platitude is.

clue.text: In vogue, it's said, and apt choice for the spelling-bee?

definitions.meaning: a fashionable word, a term everyone is saying
playfully, a word that a bee would buzz

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on 'bee': the insect buzzes, so a buzzing word would suit it.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzzword is a trendy term of the moment, and the joke reading is a word a bee might hum.

clue.text: Happening once in a blue moon? Not this occurrence

definitions.text: Happening once in a blue moon? Not this occurrence

parts.words: Happening once in a blue moon? Not this occurrence
parts.note: something that happens once in a blue moon is rare; the opposite is a thing that happens every single day

explanation.surface: A rare event is contrasted with something far more common.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyday means commonplace, occurring daily, the opposite of rare.

clue.text: Plant promissory notes on strike-breaker

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a scab is a worker who breaks a strike
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Someone slips IOUs onto a blackleg who crossed the picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb (to plant notes on someone) but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabious is a meadow flower with pincushion-like heads.

clue.text: The beast has eaten some of the pizza — don't let it take another bite

definitions.text: don't let it take another bite

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a mule is a beast of burden

indicators.note: some of signals that only a run of letters from the word is taken

explanation.surface: An animal has scoffed part of the pizza, so stop it biting again.
explanation.definitionFit: To muzzle an animal is to strap its jaws so that it cannot bite.

clue.text: Undesirable character grabbing embarrassed peer, skipped around

indicators.note: grabbing holds something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests being thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A rogue seized a red-faced nobleman and danced about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embarrassed' rearranges PEER into PERE, which goes inside CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Capered means leapt or danced about playfully, much as one skipped.

clue.text: Corrects the last part in a manuscript

parts.note: the article here is read as the indefinite article A

indicators.note: in places the ending inside the abbreviation

parts.note: the end is the last part

explanation.surface: An editor fixing the ending of a manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Amends means puts right or revises, a synonym of corrects.

clue.text: Motive for and method of constructing the footpath

parts.note: a motive is a cause
a method is a way of doing something

explanation.surface: An engineer explains why and how the path is being built.
explanation.definitionFit: A causeway is a raised road or path across wet ground.

clue.text: Insect settled on the cheese — though not for long

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece settled on another sits above it, so it is written after

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
a fly is an insect

explanation.surface: A fly lands on the Brie, though it doesn't stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefly means for a short time, so it stands for not for long.

clue.text: Carrying fruit out of sight, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: something buried is hidden underground

explanation.surface: A tree bearing fruit that cannot be seen, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Berried describes a plant bearing berries.

clue.text: A change of air at the opera

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase pointing to a song sung at the opera

indicators.note: a change of the word means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new tune played during the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: an aria is the thing heard at the opera, and 'air' also means a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera.

clue.text: With, masculine pride, Scotsman goes to his doctor

parts.note: Mac is a nickname for a Scotsman
taken as written
MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A proud Scot goes to see his GP.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is exaggerated pride in manliness.

clue.text: Mount men reshaped to be a historic record

indicators.note: reshaped means the letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Mounted men reformed to make a piece of history.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument is a structure or document that records something historic.

clue.text: Girl, we hear, the main source of trouble

indicators.note: we hear marks a sound-alike spelt differently

parts.note: a miss is a young girl
chief means main or principal

explanation.surface: A girl is apparently the root of the problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief is trouble or harm, and a mischief-maker is its source.

clue.text: A French refusal soon

parts.note: non is French for no

explanation.surface: A French person saying no to doing it straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for shortly or in a little while.

clue.text: The boon of having been unusually healthy

indicators.note: unusually means arranged in an uncommon way, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: fit means in good health

explanation.surface: The blessing of having stayed remarkably well.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is an advantage or blessing, as is a boon.

clue.text: Wizard bird!

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a marvellous bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wizard' reads like the old British slang for excellent, praising the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlin is King Arthur's magician and also a small falcon.

clue.text: About eighteen holes

definitions.meaning: one full game on a golf course

explanation.definitionFit: Around means approximately, and a round of golf covers eighteen holes.

clue.text: Tell us everything about cooked meat

parts.note: re means about or concerning
veal is meat from a calf, served cooked

explanation.surface: A demand for full details about a meat dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to disclose or make known, as when someone tells all.

clue.text: Flesh you twitch — when it lands there?

definitions.text: Flesh you twitch — when it lands there?

indicators.note: a twitch jerks things about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Your skin flinches whenever an insect alights on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: skin twitches when this insect lands on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The housefly is the common fly whose landing makes skin twitch.

clue.text: Get together a ship's company, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak marks a sound-alike of the phrase

parts.note: a crew is the company of people serving on a ship

explanation.surface: Gathering together the sailors who run a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrue is to accumulate or gather together.

clue.text: It flares up when the river rises

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Avon is an English river

explanation.surface: Something blazes when the river level goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly brightens enormously.

clue.text: Puts letters in correct order as if by magic

explanation.surface: Someone sorts letters properly as though by sorcery.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell is to write a word's letters correctly; spells are also magic charms.

clue.text: Duet with Lois interrupting it?

indicators.note: interrupting breaks things up, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A duet with Lois intrudes on a quiet moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a duet is the very thing that would break up being alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitude is being alone, which a duet with someone would interrupt.

clue.text: Ring-road terminal in Belgium

definitions.note: a phrase pointing to a place found in Belgium

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
ST, for street, is a road
the end is the terminal point

explanation.surface: The final stop of a ring road in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a Belgian port on the North Sea coast.

clue.text: Taking top off a late, overblown flower

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Taking top off a late, overblown flower' gives no parse for DAFFODIL: anagram of DOFF + A + LID would work if 'late' were 'lid', but no scan or search confirms the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Taking top off a late, overblown flower
